About me

A Public Administration graduate who writes, researches, and keeps things organized. Open any card.

I like writing that feels intentional rather than complicated, and work that is organized enough that nothing slips. Whether it is a poem, a research summary, or a client inbox, I care about clarity and the human detail.

Case studies

Two real projects, told in four parts.

Career awareness study

The challenge

Turn survey and focus-group responses from Grade 12 HUMSS students into findings a reader can act on.

The approach

Read the numbers and the comments side by side and look for repeating themes.

The work

Themes, interpretations, and recommendations written in plain language.

The outcome

A clear, readable set of findings and recommendations for the study.

Banwani

The challenge

Explain a hyperlocal procurement idea so that buyers and nearby farmers both see why it helps them.

The approach

Start from real demand: who needs produce, who grows it, and how the two are connected.

The work

Value proposition, customer journey, process map, messaging, and pitch writing.

The outcome

A refined, youth-led business concept and pitch. Banwani was named a Provincial Awardee in the Start-up Category of the Young Farmers Challenge Season 6, held by the Department of Agriculture Regional Field Office XIII.
